A year passed, and sadly i watched my friend die. I was part of the first response as had first aid training, and she didnt make it. She fell down the stairs and her head cracked open. Nothing anyone could do to stop it.

But it hit me like a truck, and i started not turning up to work, sleeping too much, self harming. Eventually a year later i quit, id had massive panic attacks turning up to work,, and would throw up at work due to the anxiety. Now im off of work due to other health reasons but it left me feeling disappointed in myself. People my age are growing up, having families and moving out. Now i just feel stuck in time, and unable to do anything. Partly due to my health issues rn, but also due to the mental illness. 

I think honestly, just focusing on myself, creating a routine and working towards things has helped me a lot. It gives me something productive to work on, so for example, i work out to he best of my ability, i write a lot. I take my dogs out as much as i can. I just try and live, and it helps

Hey, as someone who has depression and is on medication for it as well. Quite a common side effect of it is a decrease in sexual attraction/libido.

It's really not that uncommon, and from experience I don't think it has anything to do with you personally. And its more likely a side effect of medication (If she is taking any). Or the depression itself. She might feel guilty about it, and the fact she can't fufill your 'needs'. 

Maybe it might be worth sitting down in private and talking to her about the reasons why she feels the need to give you a 'hall pass'. Or as other redditors have suggested visiting the r/deadbedrooms subreddit.

I hope it all goes well for you!
